text: /// Run sync if we're in a workspace and auto-sync is enabled. Non-fatal.
/// On most events this uses the state recorded at the last sync from this
/// session's directory to skip sync when none of the files the package
/// managers named as their inputs (a lockfile, say) has changed since. Deciding
/// that reads only those files' modification times, and the workspace and
/// dependencies recorded with them are reused, so no package manager is asked
/// where the workspace is or what it depends on. If sync runs, `deps` gets populated, and later hook stages reuse
/// A sync is recorded even when a package manager failed. Its cleanup was
/// skipped, so nothing it installed was removed, and it is asked again at the
/// next `SessionStart` or once another input changes, rather than on every
/// event: a hung one would otherwise cost its timeout each time.
/// `SessionStart` runs once per session, so there we do the real work: refresh
/// every source cache (`UpdateLevel::Check`) and sync unconditionally, ignoring
/// the freshness gate, so upstream skill changes land even when the
/// Returns whether it re-synced mid-session because an input changed.

tracing::debug!("auto-sync skipped: not in a workspace");

"workspace state should have recorded the lock's mtime after first sync: {state:?}"

"workspace state mtime should be refreshed after stale cache triggers re-sync"

rationale:
**Does not hold as written: the code also syncs when there is no previous sync to compare against.** In `run_auto_sync`, for a non-`SessionStart` event with `auto-sync` on, sync is skipped only when `WorkspaceState::fresh()` returns `Some`. `fresh()` returns `None`, so sync runs, not only when a recorded input's mtime changed, but also when no sync from this directory is recorded (`last_sync` is `None`), and when the recorded sync has no inputs ("A workspace with no inputs is never fresh"). A sync that fails is not recorded either, so the next event syncs again. The requirement says "exactly when an input recorded by the previous sync has changed", which excludes those cases. `tests/init_sync.rs::auto_sync_skips_when_cargo_lock_unchanged` itself relies on the first `PreToolUse` syncing with no prior record.

What does hold (tests pass): `auto_sync_skips_when_cargo_lock_unchanged` (second `PreToolUse` with `Cargo.lock` unchanged leaves the skills dir untouched), `auto_sync_reruns_when_cargo_lock_changes` (a stale recorded mtime triggers a re-sync and refreshes the record), `tests/workspace_freshness.rs::creating_a_nested_workspace_invalidates_the_hook_workspace_cache` (passes).

To resolve: amend the text, e.g. "...MUST sync before dispatching when no sync is recorded for the directory, the recorded sync has no inputs, or an input it recorded has changed, and MUST NOT sync otherwise". Or record the no-record case as intended in some other way. Then re-judge.
requirement: On events other than `SessionStart`, when `auto-sync` is enabled, Symposium MUST sync before dispatching when, and only when, an input recorded by the workspace's last successful sync has changed or no successful sync with recorded inputs exists for it.
